 The Mandalorian and Grogu ushered in a return of Star Wars to the big screen after a seven-year break. The Jon Favreau film expanded the hit Disney+ series The Mandalorian in a theatrical release, and now you can bring the magic of the film home. Often, Star Wars brings fans plenty of books to love within the franchise. One of their most beloved releases comes from Phillip Szostak, and now fans can own their own copy of The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu ! A behind-the-scenes exploration of the art that helped create The Mandalorian and Grogu , the book includes illustrations of characters like Zeb Orrelios and Grogu, as well as a look at the impressive opening sequence that featured Mando ( Pedro Pascal ) taking out multiple AT-AT walkers.

 The Art of Star Wars books often take us deeper into the world and how some of our favorite films came to life. The Mandalorian and Grogu follows Din Djarin (Pascal) as he embarks on a journey throughout the galaxy with his adopted son, Grogu. But when Mando falls in with the Hutts as he attempts to find Rotta the Hutt ( Jeremy Allen White ), Grogu is tested on just how much he is able to do on his own without his father by his side. Including befriending a bunch of Anzellans.
 You can read more about the book in the official description: "Filled with concept art, sketches, and interviews with key cast, crew, and creatives, The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu provides readers with an exclusive look at the art created for the newest Star Wars film and the stories behind its characters, locations, and vehicles. The film stars Pedro Pascal, Sigourney Weaver , and Jeremy Allen White."
 C OLLIDER 
 Collider · Quiz 
 Collider Exclusive · 8 Questions · 2 Minutes 
 Which Star Wars Crew Should You Join? 
 Falcon · Ghost · Skeleton Crew · Razor Crest 
 Eight honest questions about how you actually are: what your friends come to you for, how you handle a night that falls apart, what you want out of work, what keeps you going. Answer them and we will tell you which ship has your seat. Four crews are hiring: the smugglers, the rebels, the kids who got hopelessly lost, and the one man who works alone until he does not. 
 🚀 Falcon (Original Trilogy) 
 👾 Ghost (Star Wars Rebels) 
 🗺️ Skeleton Crew (Skeleton Crew) 
 🪖 Razor Crest (The Mandalorian) 
 FIND YOUR CREW → 
 QUESTION 1 / 8 THE GROUP 
 01 
 What role do you play in your friend group? 
 Everybody has one, whether they admit it or not. 
 A The one who talks us out of trouble. 
 B The one who keeps everybody together. 
 C The one who suggests the bad idea. 
 D The one who turns up and fixes it. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 2 / 8 THE PACKING 
 02 
 How do you pack for a trip? 
 This says more about people than it should. 
 A Last minute, and I always forget something. 
 B Enough for me and whoever forgot theirs. 
 C One bag of nonsense and no real plan. 
 D Exactly what I need and nothing more. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 3 / 8 THE PLANS 
 03 
 Your plans collapse an hour before. What do you do? 
 Everybody reacts to this differently. 
 A Come up with something better on the spot. 
 B Get everybody on a call and sort it out. 
 C Go out anyway and see what happens. 
 D Stay in, quite happily. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 4 / 8 THE WORK 
 04 
 What would you actually want out of a job? 
 Be honest rather than impressive. 
 A Good money and nobody watching me. 
 B Work that means something, even if it pays badly. 
 C Something different every single day. 
 D Clear terms, paid on time, left alone. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 5 / 8 THE FRIENDS 
 05 
 What do people come to you for? 
 You already know which one it is. 
 A Getting them out of something. 
 B Holding it together when things get bad. 
 C Making a boring day interesting. 
 D The thing nobody else wants to do. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 6 / 8 THE ARGUMENT 
 06 
 How do you handle a disagreement with a friend? 
 This is where people differ most. 
 A Joke about it now, deal with it later. 
 B Talk it out properly, however long it takes. 
 C Forget the whole thing within an hour. 
 D Say very little, then quietly fix it. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 7 / 8 THE WEEKEND 
 07 
 What does a really good Saturday night look like? 
 No wrong answers, but there are revealing ones. 
 A Somewhere loud with people I like. 
 B A long dinner at home with my favourite few. 
 C Out with no plan at all. 
 D Quiet, alone, and completely happy about it. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 8 / 8 THE DRIVER 
 08 
 What actually keeps you going? 
 Eight questions in, this is the one that picks your crew. 
 A Freedom, and the money that pays for it. 
 B Being part of something worth fighting for. 
 C Curiosity, mostly. 
 D One person who depends on me. 
 REVEAL MY CREW → 
 Docking Clamps Released 
 Your Crew Is… 
 Four ships, four completely different reasons to be up there at all.
 Here is the one that has your seat, what flying with them would cost you, and what it would give
 back.
 Star Wars · Original Trilogy · Since 1977 
 Millennium Falcon 
 You belong on the fastest piece of junk in the galaxy, with a
 crew that took the job for the payday and then quietly stopped caring about the payday.
 Nothing on the Falcon has ever gone according to plan, and everybody aboard prefers it that
 way.
 You improvise better than you prepare, which is why you keep ending up in situations
 that a careful person would have avoided.
 The Falcon is the only ship on this list that is genuinely funny, and half of that comes
 from it breaking at the worst possible moment.
 You would pretend the whole thing is transactional right up until somebody you like is
 in trouble, and then the pretending stops instantly.
 This crew is the reason the rebellion had a chance at all, and not one of them would
 ever admit to that out loud.
 Star Wars Rebels · Disney XD · 2014 to 2018 
 The Ghost 
 You belong with the crew that turned a tiny cell of misfits into
 an actual rebellion. The Ghost is a home before it is a ship, and everybody who boards it
 arrived with something broken that the rest of them decided to look after.
 Found family is the whole engine here, and Rebels earns it by making you watch these
 people choose each other over and over again.
 You are in it for the cause, but what actually keeps you going is the four people who
 would notice immediately if you stopped showing up.
 Hera is one of the best captains in the franchise, and the show is smart enough to make
 her competence the quiet centre of everything.
 This crew pays for its wins, which is exactly what makes the wins land the way they do.
 Skeleton Crew · Disney+ · Since 2024 
 The Skeleton Crew 
 You belong with the four kids who found a buried ship, launched
 it by accident and are now extremely lost in a galaxy that eats people like them. Nobody
 here knows what they are doing, and that turns out to be the fun of it.
 Your instinct is to open the door that says do not open, and you would do it again
 tomorrow.
 Skeleton Crew is the closest Star Wars has come to an eighties adventure movie, where
 the stakes are real but the wonder never gets sanded off.
 You make friends out of whoever is standing next to you when things go wrong, which is a
 genuinely useful survival skill.
 The pirates in this one are properly frightening, and that is precisely why the kids
 being out of their depth works so well.
 The Mandalorian · Disney+ · Since 2019 
 The Razor Crest 
 You belong in the quietest ship in the galaxy, with one small
 passenger and a code you have never explained to anybody. You told yourself this was a job,
 and then it stopped being a job somewhere around the second week.
 You work alone by preference and by habit, which lasts exactly as long as it takes for
 somebody small to need looking after.
 The Mandalorian works because almost nothing gets said out loud, and the armour does the
 acting that a face usually would.
 Your loyalty is narrow and absolute, so there are very few people on your list and
 nothing will move you off it.
 The Mandalorian and Grogu took all of that to the big screen over Memorial Day 2026, the
 first Star Wars film in seven years.
 ↻ RETAKE THE QUIZ 
 More Adventures for Mando and Grogu
 Pedro Pascal as Mando with Grogu on his shoulder in The Mandalorian and Grogu. Image via Lucasfilm 
 The Mandalorian kicked Disney+ off to an exciting start as the first original series on the platform. Since then, it has remained one of the most beloved Star Wars series prior to The Mandalorian and Grogu 's release. People absolutely love watching Grogu waddle around, and now that he's growing more into his powers, he's acting more independent! It's what made The Mandalorian and Grogu so fun to watch. While The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu isn't giving us a new adventure with Din and Grogu, it is a deeper look into the franchise, and that's amazing.
 You can see the Mandalorian and his sweet son Grogu in the film The Mandalorian and Grogu on Disney+. Explore more books with a free trial of Audible . Stay tuned at Collider for more.
